extractor.note: Read every paragraph carrying transcend- (outside transcendental) or immanen-, in file order. No stratum is set: chronology.json has no entry for this commentary.

coverage_note: Term-led pass over the whole file (lines 1-384): every paragraph containing the transcendence family, including bare transcendent and immanent, was read; paragraphs without such a word were not read.

units.claim: The exclusion of objective time is the reduction in its 1905 form, with the sense of suspending transcendent positing in favour of what is given as such.
units.quote: This is the reduction in its 1905 form, two years before the Idea of Phenomenology lectures give it its name, and it already has the sense it will keep: suspension of transcendent positing in favour of what is given as such.

units.claim: The time accepted as existing is the immanent time of the flow of consciousness, not the time of the world of experience.
units.quote: We do also accept a time that exists, but it is the immanent time of the flow of consciousness, not the time of the world of experience.

units.claim: Objective space, objective time and the objective world of actual things and events are all transcendencies.
units.quote: Objective space, objective time and the objective world of actual things and events are all transcendencies.

units.claim: Transcendent here does not mean a thing in itself behind appearances; it is the transcendence of the appearing object over the experience in which it appears.
units.quote: The transcendence in question is that of the appearing object over the experience in which it appears, not that of a Kantian noumenon over phenomena.

units.claim: Brentano's theory does not stand on phenomenological ground because it works with transcendent presuppositions, existing temporal objects that cause sensations.
units.quote: It does not stand on the ground required for a phenomenological analysis: it works with transcendent presuppositions, with existing temporal objects that exert "stimuli" and "cause" sensations in us.

units.claim: An added temporal moment attached to a present content cannot explain the transcending consciousness that A is past.
units.quote: The presence of an A in consciousness, with a new moment attached, even if we call it the moment of pastness, cannot explain the transcending consciousness that A is past.

units.claim: For transcendent objects retention guarantees only that the object was perceived, not that it existed, whereas for immanent objects the retained succession is absolutely certain.
units.quote: For transcendent objects, retention guarantees only that the object was perceived, not that it existed, since perception itself can deceive.

units.claim: The editor dates the core of §22 before 1901, which shows that the distinction between immanent and transcendent evidence in time-consciousness predates the 1905 lectures.
units.quote: The editor dates the core of §22 to a sheet probably written before 1901, which shows that the distinction between immanent and transcendent evidence in time-consciousness predates the 1905 lectures.

units.claim: Every apprehension, however transcendent, is bound by the law that transcendent processes are given only as a past ending in a present limit, because their sensory basis is so given.
units.quote: The law is universal: transcendent processes are given only as a past ending in a present limit, because their sensory basis is so given.

units.claim: Three levels of constitution are distinguished: things in objective time, the immanent unities in pre-empirical time, and the absolute time-constituting flow, which is not itself a unity in time.
units.quote: second, the constituting manifolds of appearance of various levels, the immanent unities in pre-empirical time; third, the absolute time-constituting flow of consciousness

units.claim: Husserl requires distinguishing everywhere consciousness as flow, appearance as immanent object, and the transcendent object.
units.quote: We must distinguish everywhere: consciousness, which is flow; appearance, which is immanent object; and transcendent object, unless a primary content is the immanent object.

units.claim: The act of the Logical Investigations is revised into a constituted immanent unity rather than the ultimate subjective term.
units.quote: Husserl here revises his own earlier doctrine: the "act" of the Logical Investigations turns out to be a constituted immanent unity, not the ultimate subjective term.

units.claim: Acts have transcendent intentionality only through something immanently constituted, the apprehensions, so transcendent intentionality is always mediated by immanent constitution.
units.quote: Transcendent intentionality is always mediated by immanent constitution, and the relation between the two can become the object of a higher act, which is how the phenomenological attitude itself becomes possible.

units.claim: Immanent impression and perceiving are both presenting, but the immanent unity is given directly in the flow while the transcendent object is given through appearances.
units.quote: Both levels are presentings; but the immanent unity is given directly in the flow, while the transcendent object is given through appearances.

units.claim: Objective time coincides with phenomenological time because thing-apprehensions ride on temporally constituted sensory data; objective time is immanent time objectified through the apprehension of things.
units.quote: Objective time coincides point for point with phenomenological time because thing-apprehensions ride on sensory data that are themselves temporally constituted; objective time is immanent time objectified through the apprehension of things.

units.claim: There is no appearance between inner perception and its object, since the immanent object does not present itself in profiles.
units.quote: There is no appearance between inner perception and its object, since the immanent object does not present itself in profiles.

units.claim: Every consciousness is a constituted immanent unity related to its objectivity, but not every consciousness constitutes something temporal: every act is in immanent time, yet not every object is temporal.
units.quote: Every act is in immanent time, but not every object is temporal.

absences.expected_because: §34 and §37 place the absolute flow beneath the immanent unities and the transcendent object, and this section names that flow absolute subjectivity.
§13 had divided the evidence of retention by immanent and transcendent object, and this section contrasts perception with retention and recollection.
